Forme juridique de l'attributaire Le marché public sera conclu : – soit avec un opérateur économique unique ; 8/17 – soit avec un groupement d’opérateurs économiques conjoint ou solidaire. En cas de groupement conjoint, le mandataire sera solidaire, pour l'exécution du marché public, de chacun des membres du groupement, pour ses obligations contractuelles à l'égard de l’acheteur. La composition du groupement ne peut être modifiée entre la remise des offres et la date de signature du contrat. 2-6. ant indiquant qu'il ne tombe pas sous le coup d'une interdiction de soumissionner. La notification du marché public emporte acceptation du sous-traitant et agrément des conditions de paiement. Les prestations de services sont prouvées par des attestations du destinataire ou, à défaut, par une déclaration de l'opérateur économique ; • Une déclaration indiquant les effectifs moyens annuels du candidat et l'importance du personnel d'encadrement pendant les trois dernières années ; • Une description de l'outillage, du matériel et de l'équipement technique dont le candidat disposera pour la réalisation du marché public. deliverables_scope.text: reland currently uses a Microsoft Dynamics solution comprising a Customer Relationship Management system, Funding Application and Assessment Management system, End of Year Reporting system and integrated Customer Portal. references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. B2B: The DSP API and Electronic Exchange of Social Security Information (EESSI) APIs enable business-to-business integration to other Departments, public service bodies and to other European countries. Other supporting systems that make up the technology landscape include Facial Imaging Matching System (FIMS), and the General Registers Office (GRO) system. The BOMi’s scope will continue to grow in both size and complexity to (a) support the Department’s expanding Digital requirements, (b) consolidate its technology stack, and (c) continue to support new or changing legislation as it arises. The current technology platform is .NET Framework 4.x deployed to Windows Servers. In due course these will be upgraded to .NET 6 (aka .NET Core) at which time the Department will plan to deploy these systems, either for testing and/or production, on Linux/Docker when appropriate. New systems also target .NET 6 for the same purpose. The Department’s development resources are a combination of the Department’s internal staff, partnering with a number of service providers. The Senior Technical Development Advisor (TDA Lot 1) has acted as an independent strategic technical advisor across the IS Division, providing guidance on a range of SDLC and architecture related concerns. The TDA (Lot 1) helped product and platform teams deliver secure, resilient, and high-quality solutions more rapidly through the adoption of modern engineering practices and automation technologies. The TDA (Lot 1) role focused on shaping governance process and technical direction and procurement activities, translating complex technical issues into clear recommendations and implementation plans. Key areas of contribution included Continuous Integration, Release and Deployment, SDLC platform engineering, application security process and governance, Test Data Management modernisation, Developer Experience, contract testing, and SDLC platform architecture, particularly for the Department’s BOMi Platform. The TDA (Lot 1) also played a significant role in defining product and platform ownership models, associated team charters and enhanced IT governance approaches. In addition, the role supported various technical procurements through technical assessments.

The services relating to such specific contracts must be performed no later than [six] months after the expiry or termination of the FWC. Upon such notification, the parties shall use alternative means of communication until communication via electronic exchange system is restored. The provisions applicable to alternative means of communication are described in Articles II.5.3 and II.5.4 below. If the EES is temporarily unavailable, the sending party cannot be considered in breach of its obligation to send a communication within a specified deadline. In any event, for reasons linked to business continuity, the contracting authority reserves the right to use alternative means of communication at any moment. II.5.2.1 Date of communication via electronic exchange system for other than formal notifications Notifications through the EES are generally considered to have been made when they are sent by the sending party (i.e. on the date and time they are sent through the EES) as indicated by the time logs. Date of communications via mail for formal notifications Formal notifications by courier service with proof of delivery are considered to have been received on the date indicated in the proof of delivery. Our strategy sets a clear pathway to achieve net zero emissions in a way that supports our customers and ensures ESB’s continued growth. ESB are committed to leading the transition to a reliable and affordable net zero future. ESB seeks to purchase supplies, services and works that are produced or delivered in a manner that has the most positive environmental, social and economic impacts possible over their entire lifecycle. ESB procurement processes will be aligned with the standards from ISO20400, Sustainable Procurement. ESB have created a Sustainability Leadership Plan which sets out our ambitions and the actions we will take as they relate to the three pillars of sustainability - People, Planet and Place. Full details of ESB’s Sustainability Leadership Plan can be viewed here: ESB Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB requires that the successful Contractor emerging from the Procurement process be familiar with our Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB is a founding member of the Irish Supply Chain Sustainability School. The school’s aim is to support and develop skills and knowledge in sustainability in the built environment. Further

The successful tenderer will be required to work collaboratively with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop, review, test and deliver digital learning content from initial onboarding through to final approval and provision of SCORM-compliant outputs. The supplier will be expected to provide a structured and transparent development methodology, supported by appropriate governance, project management, universal design principles including accessibility, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement processes. It is proposed that the Framework will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): Create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning that keeps learner needs, content and learning objectives central to the design. Examples of digital learning topics and types include: Policy, process or compliance learning Systems, technical or operational training Bite-sized learning, such as microlearning, video or animation Develop digital learning materials using the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation) framework, ensuring learning objectives, activities and assessmen

ing objectives, activities and assessments align with Bloom’s Taxonomy and the needs of the target audience. Use purposeful interactive approaches to enhance learner engagement. Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and accessibility-by-design principles throughout, ensuring compliance with WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549 and ESB accessibility requirements, and meeting accessibility best practices. Ensure all interactive elements are accessible, usable and support diverse learner needs, undertaking additional development where required to meet accessibility requirements. Undertake accessibility testing as part of the design, development and quality assurance process, using appropriate testing methods and tools, and remediate identified accessibility issues prior to final delivery and approval. Provide appropriate coaching, guidance and instructional design support to SMEs within the business. deliverables_scope.text: ie/who-we-are/about-esb A.1.1 General Description of the Proposed Contract The Contracting Entity intends to procure a Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services framework for the provision of specialist digital learning services, including instructional design, eLearning development, accessibility reviews, project management and associated support services. The successful tenderer will be required to work collaboratively with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop, review, test and deliver digital learning content from initial onboarding through to final approval and provision of SCORM-compliant outputs. The supplier will be expected to provide a structured and transparent development methodology, supported by appropriate governance, project management, universal design principles including accessibility, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement processes. It is proposed that the Framework will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): Create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning that keeps learner needs, content and learning objectives central to the design. Positive2Work Skillnet’s Management Development Programmes also help business owners and managers improve business performance and enable businesses to achieve better results. The aim of the Positve2Work Skillnet is to enable companies to provide support and development to staff through best practice and industry relevant training. WWETB’s educational and training provision includes second-level schools, primary school, further education colleges and a range of adult and further education centres delivering education and training programmes, Post Leaving Certificate Courses (PLCs), Youthreach centres, Outdoor Education and Youth Services. WWETB places learning and the learner at the heart of its educational provision. All fakturering til Harstad kommune og samarbeidskommuner som inngår i kontrakten, må gjennomføres i Elektronisk Handels Format (EHF). Godkjente standardformater er EHF fakturering versjon 3.0 eller nyere og PEPPOL BIS (PEPPOL Business Interoperability Specification) Billing v3.0 eller nyere. Dette dokumentet omfatter bestemmelser om hvordan elektronisk fakturering gjennomføres for Harstad kommune med samarbeidskommuner, i EHF-formatet. Dokumentet beskriver kun de spesifikke informasjonselementene kommunene sender og har behov for å motta fra leverandøren. Obligatorisk innhold i EHF3.0 omhandles ikke i denne spesifikasjonen, slik som virksomhetsadresser, mva. håndtering, kontoopplysninger og lignende. Es wird erwartet, dass sämtliche Maßnahmen zur Unterstützung der Datenschutzfolgeabschätzung durch den Beauftragten durchgeführt werden. Insbesondere sind die im Verfahrensverzeichnis aufzunehmenden verfahrensbe- zogenen Angaben zur Verfügung zu stellen (vgl. Art. 30 DS-GVO). Daher werden die aktuellen techni- schen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen des Anbieters angefordert. Im Verfahren werden regelmäßig personenbezogene Daten verarbeitet. Einsatz von Unterauftragnehmern Sofern der Auftragnehmer zur Erfüllung der vertraglichen Leistungen Unterauftragnehmer als Erfüllungsgehilfen einsetzt, ist er für deren Leistungen im gleichen Maße selbst verantwortlich. Drittbeauftragung durch Unterauftragnehmer Schaltet der Unterauftragnehmer seinerseits weitere Dritte in die Leistungserbringung ein, so gilt Nr. 15.1.2 des Vertrags entsprechend. Sonstiges Gegenforderungen Der Auftraggeber ist berechtigt, mit Gegenforderungen jeglicher Art aufzurechnen. Mündliche Nebenabreden Mündliche Nebenabreden zu diesem Vertrag bestehen nicht. We ensure that Ireland's environment is protected, and we monitor changes in environmental trends to detect early warning signs of neglect or deterioration. Protecting our environment is a huge responsibility, and we work with a number of organisations that carry out specific environmental functions. As of August 2014, we are also responsible for ensuring that the people of Ireland are protected from the harmful effects of radiation. This commitment is reflected in our own activities through an Environmental Management System (EMS), certified to ISO 14001 since 2010, which supports good environmental management in our everyday operations. The EPA is an independent public body established under the Environmental Protection Agency Act, 1992. The other main instruments from which we derive our mandate are the Waste Management Act, 1996, and the Protection of the Environment Act, 2003 and Radiological Protection (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2014. references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

certifications_partner.text: o facilitate this, the Department provides an in-house “Fixture Script” library which provides a pattern. Fixture scripts can also be used within the running application, facilitating manual/exploratory testing (discussed below). The Department also provides a number of other libraries to manage fixtures. The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. Integration tests should not hard-code any officer user Ids, instead the “officer leasing” library allows an unused user/officer account to be exclusively used, with logic to automatically check/reset the officer’s certificates for signed recorded actions. Production code should never use system time directly, instead it should be possible to “mock the clock” in tests. For the BOMi application the “Programmable Clock” service provides this capability. Keeping Tests Green Whenever a project starts the Department will ensure that the initial CI pipeline for their project branch (of the Trunk) is green. Thereafter it is the responsibility of the project to keep the pipeline “green”. The Department uses a number of approaches to achieve this. B2B: The DSP API and Electronic Exchange of Social Security Information (EESSI) APIs enable business-to-business integration to other Departments, public service bodies and to other European countries. Other supporting systems that make up the technology landscape include Facial Imaging Matching System (FIMS), and the General Registers Office (GRO) system. The BOMi’s scope will continue to grow in both size and complexity to (a) support the Department’s expanding Digital requirements, (b) consolidate its technology stack, and (c) continue to support new or changing legislation as it arises. The current technology platform is .NET Framework 4.x deployed to Windows Servers. In due course these will be upgraded to .NET 6 (aka .NET Core) at which time the Department will plan to deploy these systems, either for testing and/or production, on Linux/Docker when appropriate. New systems also target .NET 6 for the same purpose. The Department’s development resources are a combination of the Department’s internal staff, partnering with a number of service providers. The Senior Technical Development Advisor (TDA Lot 1) has acted as an independent strategic technical advisor across the IS Division, providing guidance on a range of SDLC and architecture related concerns. The TDA (Lot 1) helped product and platform teams deliver secure, resilient, and high-quality solutions more rapidly through the adoption of modern engineering practices and automation technologies. The TDA (Lot 1) role focused on shaping governance process and technical direction and procurement activities, translating complex technical issues into clear recommendations and implementation plans. Key areas of contribution included Continuous Integration, Release and Deployment, SDLC platform engineering, application security process and governance, Test Data Management modernisation, Developer Experience, contract testing, and SDLC platform architecture, particularly for the Department’s BOMi Platform. The TDA (Lot 1) also played a significant role in defining product and platform ownership models, associated team charters and enhanced IT governance approaches. In addition, the role supported various technical procurements through technical assessments.

ESB seeks to purchase supplies, services and works that are produced or delivered in a manner that has the most positive environmental, social and economic impacts possible over their entire lifecycle. ESB procurement processes will be aligned with the standards from ISO20400, Sustainable Procurement. ESB have created a Sustainability Leadership Plan which sets out our ambitions and the actions we will take as they relate to the three pillars of sustainability - People, Planet and Place. Full details of ESB’s Sustainability Leadership Plan can be viewed here: ESB Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB requires that the successful Contractor emerging from the Procurement process be familiar with our Sustainable Leadership Plan. WWETB’s educational and training provision includes second-level schools, primary school, further education colleges and a range of adult and further education centres delivering education and training programmes, Post Leaving Certificate Courses (PLCs), Youthreach centres, Outdoor Education and Youth Services. WWETB places learning and the learner at the heart of its educational provision. All fakturering til Harstad kommune og samarbeidskommuner som inngår i kontrakten, må gjennomføres i Elektronisk Handels Format (EHF). Godkjente standardformater er EHF fakturering versjon 3.0 eller nyere og PEPPOL BIS (PEPPOL Business Interoperability Specification) Billing v3.0 eller nyere. Dette dokumentet omfatter bestemmelser om hvordan elektronisk fakturering gjennomføres for Harstad kommune med samarbeidskommuner, i EHF-formatet. Dokumentet beskriver kun de spesifikke informasjonselementene kommunene sender og har behov for å motta fra leverandøren. Obligatorisk innhold i EHF3.0 omhandles ikke i denne spesifikasjonen, slik som virksomhetsadresser, mva. håndtering, kontoopplysninger og lignende.
